conclusion: Six Birds Theory constructs layered descriptions of a stochastic substrate without importing Hilbert space or the Born rule. Earlier papers in the series showed that the substrate supports interference-like recombination structure on fixed support and that at least one promoted package survives on the Route A flagship family, but left open the internal status of that survivor. We classify it here on a frozen exact-finite corpus consisting of two flagship anchors, four nearby positives, matched controls, and one support-only comparison row, comparing intrinsic, sectioned, bundle-section-fiber, and protocol-indexed candidates under descended readout, signature-level descended update, second-stage recoarsening, protocol honesty, invariant validation, and exact-finite quadratic probes. The verdict is an intrinsic package: on the flagship core and required controls the intrinsic nonindexed candidate is the only candidate that combines descended readout, a nontrivial second-stage stability plateau, retained invariant and quadratic families, and protocol honesty. The nearby positives remain anchor-only on the frozen exact readout surface, but carrier diagnostics and family-level quotient evidence support an erased-partner interpretation. Weak primitive-action participation and a flagship-local exact chart are recorded as downstream, non-gating diagnostics.

Fourth, the bundle/dual and indexed routes remain comparison branches rather than final verdicts. Fifth, the formal layer is a criterion and statement surface rather than a full mechanization of the empirical atlas. Together these limitations define the boundary of the present claim: a stable intrinsic promoted package with internal structure on the frozen exact-finite surface, a nearby route that closes positively but with caveat, and downstream diagnostics that remain non-gating.
